newsitem.title: USA: PC-stocks, especially Dell, surge on bullish view.
newsitem.headline: PC-stocks, especially Dell, surge on bullish view.

text.p: Personal computer stocks soared Friday as investors viewed strong earnings from Compaq Computer Corp as bullish for the group, after a flood of technology earnings shortfall announcements this quarter.

Analysts also said that PC stocks, in particular the stock of Dell Computer Corp, were benefitting from Compaq's comments on Thursday that its new aggressively low-priced corporate PCs were not the start of a PC industry price war.
Dell Computer, which keeps hitting new highs, soared 9-3/8 to 138, another record high. A Dell spokesman said there was nothing new or substantive that would cause its stock to jump.

"There is a lot of enthusiasm for our stock," said a spokesman for Dell Computer. Traders also said there was some covering of short positions in Dell. According to NASDAQ, the short position in Dell was about 4.8 percent of its total shares outstanding, as of mid-June.

Shares of Compaq jumped 3-7/8 to 124 in heavy trading. Two analysts on Wall Street raised their earnings estimates after Compaq's better-than-expected second quarter earnings. Compaq executives also assured investors that its price cuts and its aggressively priced PCs would not hurt its profits, because its new build-to-order manufacturing method will cut costs.

"People have had the jitters for second quarter technology numbers and then Compaq comes in," said Daniel Kunstler, a JP Morgan analyst. "It's hard to find a sour note. What's going on is an interpretation, that what's going on with Compaq has got to be good for Dell too."

Other PC and PC-related stocks joining in the rally included Hewlett-Packard Co, up 2-11/16 to 61; Micron Technology Inc, maker of memory chips, up 2-1/8 to 44-7/8; and Intel Corp up two to 152-1/8. Even beleaguered Apple Computer Inc participated in the rally, soaring 15 percent. Apple added 2-1/8 to 15-3/8.

In Apple's case, investors are now breathing a sigh of relief that Gil Amelio is departing as chief executive, analysts said. "The positive outcome of all this is that the board decided to face up to what was perceived as a mistake," Kunstler said.

Traders and analysts also said PC stocks wre now beginning to trade at higher multiples. Dell is now trading at 20 to 25 times 1998 earnings estimates, compared with earlier multiples of 10 to 15 times, one of them said. "There is more confidence in their earnings," said a trader. "They are starting to trade at networking (stock) mulitples."
